intro: Visio to PDF converts Microsoft Visio diagrams into PDF. It accepts both the current VSDX format and the older VSD, so you can view organisation charts, flowcharts, network diagrams or process maps you have been sent without Visio installed, and share them with whoever needs them.

LibreOffice imports the diagram on our server, with no internet connection, and exports it as a drawing: each page of the diagram becomes a page of the PDF, and shapes, connectors and text are kept as vector elements that can be zoomed without losing sharpness. The Visio import is partial, so some stencil shapes, gradients, shadows or fonts may look different; that is why the PDF comes with a notice asking you to check it.

Choose PDF, PDF/A-2b if the diagram is part of documentation that must be preserved, or PDF/UA. With the Pages field you keep only the ones you need, for example "2" or "1-3". If the diagram contains photos or screenshots, you can set their quality and maximum resolution under more options; the Excel, PowerPoint and Word options shown there do not affect diagrams.

You can convert several Visio files at once and download them together in a ZIP. The maximum number of pages depends on your plan. If you need an exact copy of the original design, the most reliable way is to export it to PDF from Visio itself.

faq.q: What is the difference between VSD and VSDX?
faq.a: VSD is the binary format of Visio versions before 2013; VSDX is the XML-based format it has used since then. Both are converted the same way.

faq.q: Can I edit the diagram without Visio?
faq.a: The PDF cannot be edited as a diagram. To keep working on it, LibreOffice Draw opens VSD and VSDX files on your computer, with the same partial import.

faq.q: Are Visio stencils or templates accepted?
faq.a: No, only VSD and VSDX diagrams. Shape stencils (VSS and VSSX) and templates (VST and VSTX) are not supported.
